title: [Bug] Headless editor session crashes at shutdown when a GDExtension is picked up for the first time
body:
**Tested build:** Godot v4.7.2.stable.steam (Windows x64, Steam distribution), Forward+ / Vulkan locally.
**Our extension:** custom C++ GDExtension built with godot-cpp 4.7 line, registered at
MODULE_INITIALIZATION_LEVEL_SCENE, 12 classes.

## Summary

An editor session that **discovers a `.gdextension` file for the first time** crashes with
`0xC0000005` during shutdown, before the extension's own `terminate` callback runs. Only windowless
(`--headless`) sessions crash; the same project started in a windowed editor with `--editor --quit`
exits 0.

## Minimal reproduction

A project directory containing exactly three things (`<proj>` below):

```text
<proj>/project.godot              # config_version=5 + [application] config/name only
<proj>/voxel_runtime.gdextension  # entry_symbol, compatibility_minimum = "4.7", windows.editor.x86_64
<proj>/bin/libvoxelruntime.windows.editor.x86_64.dll
```

Then:

```text
# 1. cold: delete the whole cache, or just the one file
rm -rf <proj>/.godot                       # or: rm <proj>/.godot/extension_list.cfg
godot --headless --path <proj> --editor --quit
-> exit code -1073741819 (0xC0000005)      # crash, always the same instruction offset

# 2. run the same command again with nothing deleted
-> exit code 0
```

Conditions measured (each is a single-variable change, everything else left warm):

| change | result |
|---|---|
| delete only `.godot/extension_list.cfg` | crash (reproduced for 4 different projects, incl. an empty one) |
| delete only `global_script_class_cache.cfg` / `uid_cache.bin` / `editor/` + `imported/` / `.gdignore` | exit 0 |
| extension registers 0 classes (empty register_types) | exit 0 |
| extension registers 1 class (`RefCounted` subclass only) | crash |
| same session without `--headless` (windowed, `--editor --quit`) | exit 0 |
| run `--headless --recovery-mode --import` first, then the command above | exit 0 |

## Where it dies

A vectored exception handler installed from inside our dll captured this (module offsets are inside
`godot.windows.opt.tools.64.exe`; the shipped binary is stripped, so function names below are inferred
from `.pdata` function bounds plus the source paths / error literals referenced by each function body):

```text
Main::cleanup()            exe+0x603e2     (references main/main.cpp)
  MessageQueue::flush()    exe+0x3e0f032   (references core/object/message_queue.cpp)
    <61-byte thunk>        exe+0x1793055
      generate_doc_data()  exe+0x178c15c   (references editor/doc/doc_tools.cpp and its literal
                                            "Class '%s' is not exposed, skipping.")
        HashMap::_insert() exe+0x53fd842   (references core/templates/hash_map.h, "_insert")
```

`ExceptionInformation` is a **read of address 0x8**, i.e. a null base pointer plus a member offset. The
extension's `terminate` notification is never invoked, so this is not our teardown: the pending deferred
editor-documentation regeneration is executed by the `MessageQueue::flush()` at the end of
`Main::cleanup()`, at which point the extension is already unloaded and the `StringName`s of its class
names no longer have live data, and hashing such a key dereferences null.

## Expected

Either the deferred regeneration is dropped when the engine is shutting down, or the extension is
unloaded after the last deferred callback that may touch class names.

## Impact

Blocks fully automated first-run import (`--headless --import`) for any project that ships a
GDExtension; we currently have to run a `--recovery-mode --import` pass first as a bootstrap.
